resources.string: LockTime watches which app is open and closes it when its daily limit is used up. It collects nothing and sends nothing — everything stays on the phone.
Don’t allow removing or disabling LockTime
Tap an app to set limits. You can tighten them right away; loosening or removing takes effect the next day.

Protection will be removed around %1$s. After that LockTime can be uninstalled. Changed your mind? Turn the switch back on.
On: settings screens where LockTime could be uninstalled, stopped or disabled close immediately.
When on, LockTime can’t be uninstalled, stopped or disabled in settings. You can turn protection off here — it takes effect after 72 hours.
Find LockTime in the list and turn it on

It’s needed to notice when Instagram, TikTok, etc. are opened and close them when time is up.

Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → LockTime → turn on.

If the switch is greyed out with “Restricted setting”, tap “App info”, then ⋮ (top right) → “Allow restricted settings”, and come back here.
While protection is on, settings pages with LockTime (uninstall, force stop, disabling the service) close immediately.\n\nProtection can only be turned off here, and that takes effect after 72 hours.
Protection will be removed in 72 hours

You’ll be able to uninstall LockTime on %1$s.

The countdown uses an internal timer, so changing the clock won’t help. Time while the phone is off isn’t counted, and the date shifts.

Until then protection works as before. Changed your mind? Turn the switch back on to cancel the countdown.
